messages:
From: Alyssa Cheng <procurement@gammaapps.com>

Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood hosted API — vendor form + pricing breakpoints

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement here — attaching our standard vendor/PO form (Gamma_PO_Form.pdf). Before we proceed to legal review, can you confirm the following so we can complete our internal approval: 

- Do you accept PO-based purchase orders referencing a Redwood quote (we generally require PO to reference a vendor form rather than separate SOWs)?
- Clarify the per-token discount breakpoints (we need concrete thresholds for our headcount/usage forecast).
- Minimum annual or monthly commitment required to access tiered discounts?

Please fill out the vendor form or let us know if there are standard exceptions Redwood requires. We prefer to avoid long redline cycles, so a completed form + confirmation of pricing tiers would help speed things.

Attached: Gamma_PO_Form.pdf

Best,
Alyssa Cheng
Senior Procurement Manager
GammaApps



From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Cheng <procurement@gammaapps.com>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@gammaapps.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood hosted API — vendor form + pricing breakpoints

Hi Alyssa + Tom,

Appreciate the note — attaching a detailed quote (Redwood_Quote_2026-06.xlsx) and a quick summary below. We can absolutely work with a PO flow, but there are two practical constraints our legal team typically asks to handle as exceptions: limited indemnity language and data processing specifics. Instead of filing long redlines on the PO form, our usual approach is:

- Redwood signs/returns the vendor form with a small set of boilerplate exceptions (data processing appendix + liability cap), and the PO references our Master Services Agreement (link in the quote).
- If needed, we can sign a countersigned vendor form and then accept the PO against that document.

Pricing summary (annualized view, usage-based / per-token):
- Tier A: < 100M tokens/month — list price (no tier discount).
- Tier B: 100M–300M tokens/month — 15% off list per-token rate.
- Tier C: 300M–1B tokens/month — 22% off list per-token rate.
- Tier D: > 1B tokens/month — 30% off list (requires exec approval).

Commit guidance: we offer two paths:
1) Volume commit (annual) — customer commits $X spend/year and gets a flat discount applied to tokens.
2) Monthly commit banding — month-to-month usage reconciled with true-up.

For GammaApps, based on what you described on the call, recommendation: an annual commit of $500k to qualify for the 22% band. We can be flexible on band thresholds (e.g., $400k for 20%) to help you hit production ramp.

Next steps I propose:
- I can pre-fill the vendor form with company info and add our two standard exceptions (I'll attach a redline).
- If PO language is non-negotiable for you, we can accept a PO that references our quote and MSA; we'll need AP contact and invoicing instructions.

Attachments: Redwood_Quote_2026-06.xlsx (rate card & commit scenarios)

If that approach sounds ok, I can start a quick internal approval to offer a concession on the Tier C threshold for GammaApps.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: GammaApps — can we offer $500k annual commit / 22% tier?

Vivek / Marissa,

Heads-up — GammaApps procurement pushed their vendor form. I recommended $500k annual commit => 22% off per-token (Tier C). They asked for PO-first workflow and minimal redlines.

Proposed concessions to close quickly:
- Offer 22% at $500k annual commit (we can flex to $400k => 20% if needed).
- One-time onboarding credit: $25k applied in month 1 (absorbed by sales allowance).
- Add a usage true-up clause: if annual usage < 75% of committed tokens, apply a shortfall true-up at the list rate for the shortfall months.

Why: ramps look predictable; this customer could scale quickly. Margin checks: at $500k commit we're at ~35% gross margin after infra assumptions — tight but acceptable with the credit.

Approve to proceed with the 22%/500k offer and for me to sign the vendor form with our standard two exceptions?

- Lauren

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: GammaApps — can we offer $500k annual commit / 22% tier?

Lauren — go ahead with the offer but add these guardrails:

- True-up clause as you proposed (75% floor) and ability to recalibrate tiers after Q2 of the agreement.
- Limit any indemnity language to direct damages and tie to insurance limits — no broad vendor-level indemnities.
- Finance should confirm net30 terms are acceptable; if collections risk is material, require partial prepayment.

If Gamma insists on full vendor-form language with no exceptions, escalate to me before signing. Otherwise proceed and send the redline to procurement.

Vivek
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Lauren,

Thanks for the pricing summary. A few items from our side: procurement/legal cannot accept unilateral exceptions to the vendor form for key commercial terms. Our policy requires the vendor to fill and sign the form, and we do not accept reference-only MSAs — the PO must incorporate the vendor form terms. 

Concretely: 
- Please return a completed vendor form with your signature (we can accept limited redlines but they need to be inline on the form).
- Confirm minimum annual commitment language. We prefer monthly invoicing with a committed minimum (so we can budget).
- Your proposed onboarding credit is noted, but approvals are contingent on our procurement thresholds (we need documented band thresholds in the signed vendor form).

Attached: Gamma_PO_Questions.docx (we flagged specific clauses). If Redwood cannot accept our vendor form as-is, we will need to escalate and that will delay approval.

Can you return a completed form and a final quote by Wednesday EOD?

Best,
Alyssa
